fields.source_ref: the capstone prompt (W2 publishes the inputs); spec docs/graded-field-audit/w2/stimulation.json
fields.recommendation: Simplest and recommended: state the two pressures in the prompt (frac pressure 36554842.99 Pa and reservoir pressure 22468999.12 Pa at 2033.000 m TVD), which makes the field a full-precision hand-calc with no tol change. The panel change is the heavier alternative; if chosen, the tol also needs max(5e-11, 5e-10) or a more precise print.
fields.evidence: W2: Prompt only, no field moves. Field 6 needs the fracturing and reservoir pressures at the true vertical depth of 2380 m MD, which the generator interpolated from the golden survey and profiles and no lesson or panel prints (B5 finding 1). The prompt now states both at 2033.000 m TVD, with the exact acid viscosity and the mD conversion, so the Darcy ceiling of m05 l02 is a hand calculation. Keys, expected values and tolerances are unchanged. The published inputs reproduce q_max_matrix_m3s = 9.644175015204811e-05 through the vendored engines against the key 9.644175015806953e-05 (tol 5e-11); src/lib/w2PublishedInputs.test.js re-runs it.
fields.notes: Unobtainable as posed. The prompt's own sentence 'the closure stress at the true vertical depth of 2380 m measured, which is not 2380 m' points at data the learner never sees. The other five beginner fields are independent of it.

prompt_contains: The job is placed at 2380 m measured depth. At the job's true vertical depth of 2033.000 m the fracturing pressure, the closure stress there, is 36554842.99 Pa and the reservoir pressure is 22468999.12 Pa. Take the acid viscosity as exactly 0.001 Pa.s and 1 mD as 9.869233e-16 m2.
